messages:
kevin_m: Quick heads-up — I want to kick off the quant bakeoff for the new orion-7b variants (FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ). Before we run, we need a concrete plan for the calibration dataset + prompt bank. budget: ~5k tokens per model for calibration runs. goals: measure accuracy delta across QA/instruction/code and catch behavior regressions, refusal/safety drift, and formatting errors.
rita_s: Agree. My proposal: stratified prompt sampling across 6 buckets: code, math, multi-step reasoning, instruction-following, conversational QA, and safety/refusal. ~2k prompts total, but we can sample down to 800-1k for fast iter. Make sure to include paraphrases and temperature variants.
jacob_w: +1. For sampling, we should weight by real traffic: product logs show code ~18%, instr-following ~35%, convo QA ~22%, others split. We'll mirror that distribution for the main bank, then create a stress set that's heavy on edgecases.
kevin_m: Good. Important constraints: 1) calibration set must not overlap with our public evals or training holdouts; 2) include token-length stratification (short <20, medium 20-200, long >200); 3) add markup/structure tests (tables, JSON output).
rita_s: For paraphrases, we can use 3 paraphrases per prompt using back-translation + in-house paraphrase model. For instruction polymorphism, include both terse and verbose phrasings.
jacob_w: I'll produce SQL to extract candidate prompts from the corpus. Example filter:
```
SELECT id, text, domain, length_tokens FROM prompts
WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01' AND domain IN ('code','instr','chat','math','safety')
AND id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM public_eval_holdout)
ORDER BY RANDOM()
LIMIT 2000;
```
kevin_m: Nice. Metrics we should compute per-model and per-domain: Exact-match (where applicable), normalized edit-distance, bertscore/embedding-sim for open answers, and a delta pass rate for safety/refusal. Also a manual spot-check of top regressions (10 per domain).
jacob_w: For code tasks, add execution-based checks where possible (python runner sandbox) and measure AST-level diffs. For math, add symbolic comparison for simple algebra.
rita_s: On the calibration side, do we want to run with the same temperature/decoding across quant variants? I suggest: greedy + topp=0.9 for sampling variants. Keep sampling seed fixed for repeatability.
kevin_m: Keep decoding consistent. Also capture logits for the calibration tokens when possible so we can compute per-layer KL and logit-scale shifts for debugging.
jacob_w: Deployment profile note: we'll produce two calibration slices — latency-focused (short prompts, batch size 1, min-latency kernels) and throughput-focused (longer prompts, batching simulation). That helps choose INT8 vs GPTQ vs AWQ per profile.
rita_s: We should tag each prompt with labels: domain, length_bucket, safety_flag, structured_output_required, exec_check (bool), paraphrase_source. Keep as CSV/TSV for the eval harness.
eval-bot: Scheduled job created: quant-bakeoff/orion-7b/2025-03-04T03:00Z — will run calibration slice (800 prompts) across all quant formats and post results to /quant-results/orion-7b/1769504321.
kevin_m: Tasks: jacob - generate candidate dump + SQL filters by EOD; rita - curate final 800 prompt bank and paraphrase set by Wed; I'll wire up the metrics and manual review checklist. eval-bot - run and upload logs.
jacob_w: I'll also attach sampling seeds and the script for stratified downsampling so the results are deterministic.
rita_s: One more: include a small anti-overfit set where we purposely insert prompts from recent model failures to see if quantization amplifies them. 50 prompts injected.
kevin_m: Perfect. Let's reconvene after first pass graphs. Quick note: include failures as short snippets in the 1st reply message so it's easy to triage. :thumbsup:
rita_s: Sounds good, I'll create the CSV with columns: id, text, domain, length_bucket, safety_flag, paraphrase_group, exec_check, sampling_seed. Will push to s3://redwood-evals/orion/calib/ by Wed.
kevin_m: Thanks — assigning.
(automated) eval-bot: Job quant-bakeoff/orion-7b queued by kevin_m — will post run summary when complete.
